slides.title: What we chose, why, and how we checked it
params: Locked in the pre-registration; the same value in all 24 arms and all controls
The repeat is the resampling unit for inference; folds are not independent
fold-level intervals reported as a conservative variant
Keeps the comparison about topology, not about the weight scale
Equal prevalence across labels inside an arm (D-11)
the uncapped primary design is also reported
Approved symbol wins; previous symbols mapped only when unambiguous
ambiguous symbols are dropped and counted (83 for NCG)
slides.honesty: We never picked a parameter to make a result significant. The parameters were frozen before the analysis; every later change is an amendment in docs/pre_registration_amendments.md, and robustness is shown with hub-capped RWR, the alpha sweep, the per-network cap, complex-aware cross-validation and a per-cancer-type split.
slides.footer: Take-home: the frozen design plus five sensitivity analyses is the robustness argument — not a favourable p-value.

slides.title: The primary endpoint: 23 of 24 arms positive
stats: best arm: STRING physical x OT no-lit
only negative arm: Reactome x newest drivers
slides.note: The pre-registered H1 rule (95 % CI excludes 0 in every arm) is met under four of five interval constructions (24/24) and NOT met under the conservative gene-cluster interval (20/24) — the four exceptions are all the newest-driver label.
slides.footer: Take-home: the prior clearly beats degree — the interesting question is how much of that survives the next three slides.

slides.title: Where the prior's stability comes from — and where it does not
bullets: Per-gene scores are unstable (median CV 18 %; a median gene moves ~270 ranks) while the arm-level mean is stable (SD 0.0047).
The instability is the gene's own score variance (rho = 1.00, q = 2e-137); no classical topology descriptor predicts it.
Network-level stability is predicted by coverage and the 2-core fraction (rho = -0.905, q = 0.012) — not by size, density or modularity.
The mechanism is the seed-count law: RWR weights seeds linearly, so bagging the prior is a provable no-op. Regularising it cannot restore the ranking.
slides.footer: Take-home: the prior's instability is not a topology effect — it is the gene's own score variance, and it cannot be smoothed away.

slides.title: External evidence, and the fragility of our own numbers
bullets: DepMap (1,361 cell lines): at K = 30 candidates the prior shows no enrichment beyond chance (6 % of cell lines, p < 0.05); at K = 100 it does (48 %). The prior carries set-level signal, not gene-level calls.

NCG arbitration: the prior ranks drivers that our labels do not contain above the rest in 24/24 arms (median +0.041) — but in only 13/24 on the low-FPR endpoint, and the protein networks are the only ones that pass.
Our own negative set: 10-22 % of the held-out 'negatives' are curated NCG drivers. Removing them halves the IntOGen margin (0.065 -> 0.030) and raises the Open Targets margin (0.085 -> 0.103).
Reactome is positive on the 2019 NCG catalogue (+0.089) but negative on the two newest catalogues — the failure is label-specific, not network-specific.
slides.footer: Take-home: the prior really transfers to drivers we never labelled — but the absolute numbers depend on how the negative set is built.

slides.title: What the benchmark says about network priors
points: A network prior contributes signal beyond node degree
23/24 arms positive; the pre-registered rule met under four of five interval constructions
The contribution is real but modest and label-dependent
median +0.081; 10-22 % of the 'negatives' are curated drivers; cleaning them halves the strictest-label margin
Much of the published margin is study visibility
a bait-matched null removes most of the enrichment, and the temporal label's advantage collapses to +0.002
gene-level CV is explained by the gene's own score variance (rho = 1.00); bagging the prior is a provable no-op
Curated networks fail on recently discovered drivers
Reactome is +0.089 on the 2019 catalogue and negative on the two newest ones — a coverage and curator-lag effect
slides.footer: Take-home: network priors help, modestly and unevenly — the honest number is more useful than the headline one.

slides.title: What would change our mind
limits: The gene-cluster interval fails in 4 of 24 arms
run the benchmark on an independent cell-line-derived label (DepMap essential genes) with the same protocol
Our negative set contains curated drivers
re-derive the background from NCG and ClinGen with explicit exclusion, then re-run the factorial
The prior is evaluated on its own ranking
a blind challenge: a held-out expert panel ranks the same genes, as in Boutros et al. 2014
perturbation experiment: edit the seed set of a driver and measure the effect on the predicted neighbourhood
re-run the locked protocol with a second fixed learner (closeness centrality) to show the conclusion is not learner-specific
slides.footer: Take-home: every limitation we know of has a named experiment attached to it.
